title: NeuroDance – Ameliorating the symptoms and promoting the well-being in patients with Parkinson's Disease (PD) and related disorders
summary:
The research project investigates how dance can improve mobility, balance, and well-being in individuals with Parkinson’s disease. During a five-month dance intervention, participants take part in guided dance sessions twice a week. The effects of the program are scientifically evaluated before and after the intervention. Measurements include mobility, gait, and balance, as well as quality of life and fear of falling. In addition, electrical brain and muscle activities are recorded to gain insights into how dance influences motor processes in the brain.
The aim of the study is to demonstrate that dance training not only enhances physical mobility but also sustainably improves emotional well-being and quality of life in people living with Parkinson’s disease.
conditions: Morbus Parkinson’s syndrome (stages 1–4 according to Hoehn & Yahr)

interventions.name:
Intervention group:
Attendance in a dance intervention. (2 weekly sessions of 60 minutes over 18 weeks)
Passive control group: no attendance in a dance intervention (no intervention)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Diagnosed Parkinson’s disease (Hoehn and Yahr stages 1 to 4)

Comprehension of verbal and action-related instructions.
Exclusion criteria:
Diagnosed Parkinson’s disease, Hoehn and Yahr stage 5

Severe cognitive impairment (MoCA ≥ 21 points)
